items.title: Preview approved Common companions in existing detail screen
items.quote: "Ok" [to preparing a test version of companion-detail screens using already approved sprites and habitat backgrounds].  "Yeah I like all the ones so far that are there."

asks.text: The lunge now repeats every 4 seconds, the same timing as the tutorial, and a tap plays it at once. I think it suits the page. If it feels busy while you read stats, 6 seconds would be calmer.

Every companion except the starters now gets a soft glow, three sparkles and a strike flash in its category's colours, placed a bit differently each time. I kept it to three sparkles, the same as the starters, so the page stays calm. A Rare or higher companion could get one or two extra sparkles later if you want them to feel more special.

Mortals, Spirits and Aberrations had no strike flash in the tutorial, so I gave them one in the same style: a gold diamond for Mortals, a pale star for Spirits and a jagged violet shard for Aberrations.
Size and weight are removed everywhere. The tutorial's "A NEW BOND" screen now shows the starter's short description in that spot instead of leaving it empty.

I picked one scene for each new Common: Reedwatch Tinker with Wetland Reeds, Millward Bellkeeper with Ancient Gate, Dewfern with Fungal Hollow, Coppice Cricket with Thorn Bramble and Unstitch with Rift Fracture. They're only on the preview page. Tell me which pairs you like and I'll make them those companions' backgrounds in the game.

items.title: Haven 3.0–4.0: upgradeable town and endless connected frontier
items.quote: "Ok what about the progress knight code what if we used that to replace the arena"  "Yeah I'm saying complelty replace arena"

asks.text: The request asks for phone screenshots and a short recording of the title, the static and the framed town. Nobody can take them from the build robot. I suggest Noah takes them on the test site, or asks for a local Claude session to take them.

Main has workflow-file and status-tool changes that this branch doesn't have. They don't touch the game. I'm not allowed to push workflow-file changes, so the hourly update robot or Noah needs to bring them in.

The static wipe lasts 0.6 seconds: about 0.15 s of plain static, then a scanline sweeps down over 0.45 s. That's in the middle of the 0.4–0.8 s you asked for, and I think it feels like a screen switching on without slowing you down.
The title shows once each time the game is opened or reloaded. Closing and reopening Haven doesn't show it again. I think that's right: more often would get in the way.

The HAVEN and PRESS START letters are pixel letters I drew in code, not a copied console font or logo. The shell is purple-grey plastic, like an old handheld, and the top strip says LOREBOUND, not a console name.

I kept the decorations to the top strip and left the sides and bottom at 5px, so the town loses only about 28px of height. If you'd like a chunkier handheld, with a real cross pad and buttons under the screen, it would cost about 60–80px of the town's height on a small phone. I'd keep it thin.
Inside the frame, Haven's screen edge is now a dark bezel line instead of the thin gold border, so it reads as a screen inside the shell. The panels inside keep their gold edges.

items.title: Set 0.2-second Auto Summon and replace Tome opening with Rift spin-up
items.quote: during auto summons it goes back to .5 seconds per companion. Also the tome animation needs to be removed when opening one at a time. I think it should be replaced with the portal gif spinning up faster than having the screen pop up.

asks.text: A tap on the Rift now spins it up for 0.3 seconds before the result opens. I think that's a good length: it feels quick, but you still see it. In 0.3 seconds the swirl turns one and a half times, so it ends quite fast. If it looks like a flicker on your phone, I'd make it one full turn instead.

I kept the shorter effect for repeats that the game already had: repeat Commons and Uncommons play at a bit under half the length, and new or Rare-and-up companions get the full effect. That's what you asked for, so I didn't make it any shorter.
